## Why This Is Asked
Realistic security instrumentation for CNFs requires tenant isolation at the policy layer and runtime enforcement without downing services.

## Key Concepts
- CNFPolicy CRD for per-tenant TLS constraints
- In-sidecar dynamic policy loading and hot-reload
- TLS version negotiation, cipher suite hardening, SNI validation, HSTS
- Audit trails and rollback safety

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal CNFPolicy CRD (schematic)
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: cnfpolicies.cnf.example.com
spec:
  group: cnf.example.com
  versions:
    - name: v1
      served: true
      storage: true
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: cnfpolicies
    singular: cnfpolicy
```

```yaml
apiVersion: cnf.example.com/v1
kind: CNFPolicy

  name: tenant-a-tls

  minCipher: \"ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256\"
  hsts: true
  tlsSNIValidation: true
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
- Validates understanding of namespace-scoped quotas and limits, a core tenancy control pattern in multi-tenant Kubernetes environments.

## Key Concepts
- ResourceQuota: Enforces aggregate resource limits across a namespace
- LimitRange: Defines default requests/limits and validates pod resource specifications
- Per-namespace isolation: Ensures tenants cannot exceed allocated resources
- Quota enforcement: Kubernetes rejects pods that would exceed quota limits
- Validation methods: kubectl describe quota and limitrange commands

## Code Example
```yaml
# Namespace: cnf-tenant-A
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: cnf-tenant-A

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: cnf-tenant-A-quota
  namespace: cnf-tenant-A
spec:
  hard:
    limits.cpu: 4
    limits.memory: 16Gi
    requests.cpu: 2
    requests.memory: 8Gi

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: cnf-tenant-A-limits
  namespace: cnf-tenant-A
spec:
  limits:
  - default:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 512Mi
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
    type: Container
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates advanced telemetry architecture, per-tenant observability, dynamic sampling strategies, and operational safety practices for CNF gateways at scale.

## Key Concepts
- OpenTelemetry, OTLP, trace context propagation, and baggage
- Namespace-scoped configuration and feature flags
- Adaptive sampling policies with latency-aware thresholds
- Canary rollouts and rollback safety

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf.trace
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  cnf.trace.enabled: "true"
  cnf.trace.sample-rate: "0.25"
  cnf.trace.target: "otel-collector.tenant-a.svc.cluster.local:4317"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 0
      maxSurge: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: cnf-gateway
        image: cnf-gateway:latest
        env:
        - name: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: cnf.trace
              key: cnf.trace.target
      - name: otel-collector
        image: otel/collector:latest
        args: ["--config=/etc/otel/config.yaml"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: otel-config
          mountPath: /etc/otel
      volumes:
      - name: otel-config
        configMap:
          name: otel-collector-config
```

## Adaptive Sampling Implementation
```go
func AdaptiveSampler(sampleRate float64, errorRate float64) float64 {
    baseRate := sampleRate
    if errorRate > 0.05 {
        return min(1.0, baseRate*2)
    }
    return baseRate
}
```

## Rollout Strategy
```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
      - setWeight: 5
      - pause: {duration: 5m}
      analysis:
        templates:
        - templateName: error-rate-check
        successfulRunHistoryLimit: 3
```

## Why This Is Asked

- Observability hooks for validation during rollout phases

## Code Example
```yaml
# (a) Tenant Routing Policy with Canary Weight and Rollout Window
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: TenantRoutePolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-api-v2
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  tenant: tenant-a
  targetCluster: cluster-west
  route:
    path: /api/v2
    backendRefs:
      - name: gateway-service
        port: 8080
  canary:
    weight: 0  # Start at 0%
    rolloutDuration: 30m
    stepWeight: 10  # Increment by 10% each step
    stepInterval: 5m
  rollback:
    enabled: true
    failureThreshold: 5  # Rollback if 5 consecutive errors exceed threshold
    errorRateThreshold: 0.05  # 5% error rate triggers rollback
  healthCheck:
    endpoint: /healthz
    interval: 30s
    timeout: 10s
---
# (b) Sidecar Config to Watch Policy and Push Updates
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: envoy-gateway-sidecar
  namespace: gateway-system
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: xds-controller
          image: cnf/xds-controller:latest
          args:
            - --policy-namespace=tenant-a
            - --xds-address=$(POD_IP):18000
            - --sync-interval=10s
          env:
            - name: POD_IP
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef:
                  fieldPath: status.podIP
          volumeMounts:
            - name: policy-config
              mountPath: /etc/policy
              readOnly: true
        - name: envoy
          image: envoyproxy/envoy:latest
          args:
            - --config-path /etc/envoy/envoy.yaml
            - --service-cluster gateway
          volumeMounts:
            - name: envoy-config
              mountPath: /etc/envoy
      volumes:
        - name: policy-config
          configMap:
            name: tenant-policies
        - name: envoy-config
          emptyDir: {}
---
# (c) One-Namespace Test Manifest for Canary Rollout and Rollback
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: CanaryRolloutTest
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-canary-test
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  policyRef:
    name: tenant-a-api-v2
  testStages:
    - stage: baseline
      duration: 5m
      expectedWeight: 0
      checks:
        - type: metrics
          metric: requests_total{path="/api/v2"}
          condition: equals 0
    - stage: canary_10pct
      duration: 10m
      expectedWeight: 10
      checks:
        - type: http
          url: http://gateway.tenanta.svc/health
          expectSuccessRate: 0.95
        - type: metrics
          metric: envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_xx{cluster="backend-v2"}
          condition: exists
    - stage: canary_50pct
      duration: 10m
      expectedWeight: 50
      checks:
        - type: http
          url: http://gateway.tenanta.svc/api/v2/users
          expectSuccessRate: 0.99
    - stage: full_rollout
      duration: 5m
      expectedWeight: 100
      checks:
        - type: http
          url: http://gateway.tenanta.svc/api/v2/**
          expectSuccessRate: 0.999
  rollbackTest:
    enabled: true
    triggerFailureAt: canary_50pct
    expectedBehavior: weight_reverts_to_0_within_2m
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests capability to design advanced per-tenant control planes in CNF gateways, focusing on feature-flag rollouts, canary traffic, and safe rollback at scale.

## Key Concepts

- Tenant-scoped CustomResourceDefinition (CRD)
- Canary and hash-based traffic split per tenant
- Mutual-TLS gRPC reporting to control plane
- Sliding-window error/latency thresholds for rollback
- Minimal manifests to validate end-to-end

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: tenantrollouts.cnf.example.com
spec:
  group: cnf.example.com
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              tenantID:
                type: string
              featureFlag:
                type: string
              rolloutPercent:
                type: integer
              fallbackBehavior:
                type: string
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: tenantrollouts
    singular: tenantrollout
    kind: TenantRollout
    shortNames: [ tr ]
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you model rollback triggers across tenants if telemetry is noisy? 
- What instrumentation would you add to guarantee deterministic routing and auditability?
